title: Capacity Fit Matrix & SLO Negotiation Cheatsheet for Dedicated Reservations
creator: Priya Narayanan
description:
This ticket captures a compact, customer-facing cheatsheet and internal rubric for assessing enterprise dedicated capacity requests. The goal is to speed intake calls, produce consistent SLA bounds (latency/availability/throughput), recommend a GPU class, and propose scaling policies that balance cost predictability with burst flexibility. The output will be a short matrix + negotiation guidance used by Solutions, Sales, and PMs during intake and by Eng for sizing and onboarding.

What's included: a 4x4 capacity-fit matrix (workload profile x latency target), a scoring system (0-10) across signals (RPS, tokens/sec, concurrency, prompt length distribution, KV cache hit-rate), GPU class guidance (T4 / A10 / A100 / H100 / LLM-optimized instances), recommended reserved throughput bands and guardrails for burst credits, and two canned scaling policies (conservative-reserved, elastic-reserved-with-burst). It also includes a short negotiation cheat sheet mapping customer asks to a recommended commitment band or alternative mitigation (model quantization, batching advisories, caching expectations).
acceptance_criteria: One-page customer-facing cheatsheet PDF exported to Drive
Internal rubric documented in Confluence with worked examples for 3 customer archetypes (chatty low-latency, batch embeddings, high-throughput inference)
Engineering has signaled feasibility for recommended buffer/headroom numbers and GPU mapping
Sales/Solutions reviewed and approved negotiation language and fallback options
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya: Created initial stub after two intake calls where sizing diverged wildly; drafted matrix and scoring fields.
2026-03-11 Ethan: Added GPU mapping notes (prefer H100 for sustained high throughput; A100 for latency-sensitive but lower concurrency; T4/A10 for cost-sensitive bursty workloads).
2026-03-12 Ana (Solutions): Suggested adding a 'KV cache effectiveness' multiplier to reduce recommended reserved throughput by up to 30% for high-cache-hit workloads.

2026-03-13 Eng-Infra sync: ENG-19842 owner confirmed autoscaler can support 'burst credits' semantics but needs fallbacks for preemptible GPUs. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/419
2026-03-14 Priya: Incorporated feedback and produced draft cheatsheet. Shared to #sales-solutions and request for formal review from SRE and Pricing.
2026-03-14 Review note (SRE - Jordan): Recommended default healthcheck and circuit-breaker templates for canary period; called out 2-minute rollout windows for capacity changes.
decision: Use a score-first intake: compute workload score from customer inputs; scores 0-3 => Band C (cost-optimized, recommend T4/A10), 4-6 => Band B (balanced, recommend A100), 7-10 => Band A (performance SLOs, recommend H100 or LLM-optimized instances). Default reserved throughput = baseline RPS * 1.25 + headroom token buffer. Offer burst credits up to 50% for Band B and 100% for Band C with strong caveats. Autoscaling policy: target 95% utilization of reserved pool, with predictive scaling windows for predictable traffic patterns.
